candidate.title: RIP-Seq
candidate.scope: Illumina’s assigned RIP-Seq schematic, verified against the collection heading RIP-Seq: RNA Immunoprecipitation Sequencing and caption A schematic overview of RIP-seq. One depicted route selects RNA-protein complexes by immunoprecipitation, applies RNase digestion, extracts the retained RNA, and makes cDNA. The far-left RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP) icon is a detached descriptive overview, not a second workflow or extra operation. The cDNA endpoint represents selected RNA sequence; adapter addition, amplification, sequencing and mapping are not drawn as operations. Zhao et al. (2010) establishes the native RIP-seq family and the shared immunoprecipitation-to-cDNA interface, but its reported library preparation does not establish the depicted RNase-protection selection or the catalogue single-base binding-site claim. The graph preserves the catalogue depiction, with these paper-based limitations made explicit.

operations.label: Immunoprecipitate RNA-protein complex
operations.description: Antibodies directed against the protein of interest select RNA-protein complexes from the input material. The output retains associated RNA together with the selected protein complex. Magenta antibody symbols illustrate this operation; the detached far-left RIP overview is not an additional immunoprecipitation.
operations.mechanism: Antibody-mediated immunoprecipitation of the target protein and associated RNA; antibody is a selection reagent, not an RNA-derived product.
operations.information_effect: Introduces enrichment for RNA associated with the selected protein complex. Nonspecific antibody capture and unstable complexes limit specificity and recovery; selection does not prove direct binding of every recovered RNA to the antibody target.

operations.label: RNase digestion

The cited primary paper reports RNase tests as controls and does not substantiate this library-selection step.

method_scopes.rationale: The card title and verified collection heading/caption identify one target, RIP-Seq (RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing). All four operations apply to this declared Illumina schematic. The arrows show a single retained-material route; there is no branch, pooling step or depicted alternative method. The detached RIP icon names the immunoprecipitation component. The RNase-containing depiction belongs to the catalogue’s RIP-Seq presentation; it is not evidence that all native RIP-seq implementations, including Zhao’s, have this preparation history. The cited native implementation supports protein-directed RNA capture and cDNA readout, while its nuclease experiments are controls. Template switching, UV-crosslink validation, MAPS and iCLIP mentioned in sources do not become additional targets or drawn operations.
